description.main: Autumn/Winter 2026–2027 issue of Apartamento, with Dozie Kanu at home in the Portuguese countryside, Constance Debré in Paris, Anupama Kundoo, Julian Schnabel, Peaches, Martine Syms, Gerard Malanga, and an essay by Jocko Weyland.
description.extended:
Autumn/Winter 2026–2027, with Dozie Kanu at home in the Portuguese countryside, Constance Debré in Paris, Anupama Kundoo, Julian Schnabel, Peaches, Martine Syms, Gerard Malanga, and an essay by Jocko Weyland.

The cover story is Camille Okhio's conversation with the American artist Dozie Kanu at Azoia de Cima, where he lives and works, photographed by José Pedro Cortes. They cover his move from New York to Portugal, his Nigerian heritage, and the fire in his live/work space just before a shoot for Knoll. In Paris, contributing editor Jina Khayyer interviews the writer Constance Debré on love, desire and boredom, and Osma Harvilahti photographs her apartment, which has no full bath. The issue also features Dave Baby, Joey Arias, Rodney Mullen, Filip Pągowski, Go Hasegawa, Darina Allen, and Hannes Van Severen and Fien Muller, and returns to Anupama Kundoo's Hut in Petite Ferme. Peter Hanley's "The Culinary Academy of the Pyrenees, On Tour!" runs with illustrations by Oscar Grønner, Anna Herms writes an ode to Inge Mahn, and Weyland's essay is "Wei Xing Doesn't Skate".

Jocko Weyland first appeared in Apartamento in issue 3, in 2009, and his book The Powder is held in this library, as are Julian Schnabel's Draw A Family and Polaroids.
